clue.text: Dismiss expert screening river fun run

parts.note: to dismiss an employee is to sack them
R is the map abbreviation for river
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: An organiser sends away a specialist who was checking the river before a charity jog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screening' has the expert wrapped round the river. The definition is playful: a school sports day event run for laughs.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful description of the sports-day contest in which children hop along inside bags.

clue.text: View Pluto rising close to Neptune

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the god's name is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Dis is another name for Pluto, Roman god of the underworld

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, here taken from Neptune

explanation.surface: An astronomer watches Pluto come up near Neptune in the night sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns DIS upwards to give SID, and 'close to' takes the last letter of Neptune. Pluto is the god, not the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an aspect or angle of a matter, as in looking at every angle of a question.

clue.text: After prayer, golden couples bury small trinkets

indicators.note: After says the gold-and-couples part follows the prayer

parts.note: a collect is a short prayer in Anglican and Catholic services

indicators.note: to bury something is to cover it over, so the two outer pieces close over the small letter

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
two people in a relationship are an item, so couples are items
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Once prayers are said, pairs of gilded lovers put little keepsakes in the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' sets the order and 'bury' makes the gold and the couples close over the small letter. The surface suggests a burial; the answer's apostrophe is ignored in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: small ornaments and curios are the sort of thing enthusiasts hunt for and hoard.

clue.text: Nice article found in pair of lines? Just kidding

indicators.note: found in places the French word between the two line words

parts.note: a rail is a line of track, the first of the two
Ry is an abbreviation of railway, the second line
le is 'the' in French, as spoken in the city of Nice

explanation.surface: Someone spots a pleasant piece in a couplet and then admits they were only joking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' sits the article between two different words for a line. Nice is the French city, so its article is French, not a pleasant piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: good-humoured teasing, banter that is only in fun.

clue.text: Banter from winger that's not kept in check

indicators.note: not kept says the letters that follow are dropped from the bird's name

parts.note: a chaffinch is a bird, a creature with wings
taken as written
ch is the chess notation for check

explanation.surface: A footballer on the flank keeps up a stream of unrestrained teasing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's not kept' drops IN and CH from the bird. The winger is no footballer, and 'in check' is two pieces, not a phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: light-hearted teasing talk.

clue.text: Film director with a good score when shooting

definitions.meaning: Michael, the British director of Death Wish
a shot that takes the point outright in tennis, or the deciding goal in football

explanation.definitionFit: Both a surname from British cinema and the term for a decisive shot in sport.

clue.text: Disgrace one left out of popular family

parts.note: something popular is in, meaning in fashion

indicators.note: out of says the two letters before it are removed from the family

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Shame falls on someone who was cut out of a well-liked household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes two adjacent letters from the household word; 'left' is the abbreviation, not what remains. 'popular family' looks like one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: public shame or ill repute.

clue.text: NHS residents age after surgery for eye complaint

indicators.note: surgery cuts things up and puts them back differently, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: People in a British state-run care home grow old following operations on their eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after surgery' is the anagram signal, covering all three words before it. The NHS is Britain's National Health Service, which makes the surface so natural.
explanation.definitionFit: Another name for myopia, a condition where distant things look blurred.

clue.text: Rhode island firm, tricked out of article, bounced back

parts.note: RI is the postal abbreviation for the US state
Co is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: out of says the tricked word loses the article named next

parts.note: someone tricked has been cheated
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A New England company, swindled out of a piece of merchandise, recovered well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes A from CHEATED, leaving CHETED.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: rebounded off a surface, as a bullet does.

clue.text: Naive commercial about large plastic tube

indicators.note: about puts the first two pieces around the large letter

parts.note: a raw recruit is naive and inexperienced
a plug is a piece of promotion, an advert
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A simple-minded advert is made concerning a big piece of piping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the two words round the size letter. The answer is a British trade name for the sleeve pushed into a drilled hole to grip a screw.
explanation.definitionFit: A description of the hollow fixing that lines a wall hole so a screw holds.

clue.text: A Somalia boy, not so backward, finding top monk

indicators.note: backward says the whole run of pieces is read from right to left
not so tells you to drop the letters S and O from the country

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A youngster from Somalia, less slow than supposed, tracks down a senior holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not so' cuts SO from Somalia and 'backward' turns A MALIA LAD round to give the answer. The phrase 'not so backward' reads as one but splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of the spiritual head of Tibetan Buddhism.

clue.text: Guinea coin smuggled into football club

indicators.note: into puts the smuggling word inside the club's letters

parts.note: FC is the usual abbreviation, as in Liverpool FC
to run guns or drugs is to smuggle them, so smuggled is ran

explanation.surface: An old gold piece is sneaked into a soccer team's ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' is the insertion signal. Guinea is the West African country, not the old British gold coin worth 21 shillings, which the smuggling story wants you to picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The currency unit of the West African republic.

clue.text: Fine extension: hide collapsed floor

definitions.meaning: as a noun, an animal's skin or pelt
the past tense of tumble down
as a verb, to knock someone to the ground

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
an ell is a wing built at right angles onto a building

explanation.surface: A nice new wing on the house conceals a floor that has caved in.
explanation.walkthrough: After the wordplay come three separate definitions in a row, each a different sense of the same short word.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: an animal pelt, tumbled down, and to knock over.

clue.text: Traditional notes of musk oil mixed in case of fabric

indicators.note: in places the mixed letters inside the outer pair from fabric
the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters
mixed tells you the two words before it are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned perfume scents of musk oil are blended inside a cloth wrapper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' turns MUSK OIL into OLKMUSI, and 'in case of' puts that inside F and C, the first and last letters of fabric. The notes are musical, not scents.
explanation.definitionFit: Songs and tunes handed down among ordinary people over generations.

clue.text: Plump for ripping new option: MBE!

indicators.note: ripping tears things apart, so the letters after it are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new, as on maps

explanation.surface: Someone enthusiastically chooses a splendid fresh choice: a British honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ripping' rearranges N, OPTION and MBE. 'Plump for' looks like the verb meaning choose, but Plump alone is the definition; an MBE is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A word from French used as an adjective meaning stout or well-rounded.

clue.text: Doctor to reuse missing English vehicle

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor

indicators.note: missing says the reuse word lacks the letter named next

parts.note: to recycle something is to reuse it

explanation.surface: A medic is going to use a foreign-made car again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' removes the first E from RECYCLE, leaving RCYCLE. 'Doctor' is not an anagram signal here.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a two-wheeled powered machine is one kind of transport.

clue.text: Second person supported by new agent and boyfriend

indicators.note: in a down entry, the piece supported sits on top of the ones holding it up

parts.note: in grammar the second-person pronoun is you
a G-man is American slang for an FBI agent

explanation.surface: A runner-up is backed by a fresh representative and her partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supported by' stacks YOU above N and GMAN. Second person is the grammatical term, not someone who came second.
explanation.definitionFit: A slightly old-fashioned term for a woman's sweetheart.

clue.text: Old letter s

definitions.note: the letter stands for its own shape, a double curve

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old, as in OT
gee is the spelt-out name of the letter G

explanation.surface: An ancient character from the alphabet, the letter s.
explanation.walkthrough: The lone 's' is the definition: it pictures the shape. The answer is an architectural term for such a curve.
explanation.definitionFit: A moulding or arch line with a double curve shaped like that character.

clue.text: Result of cutting about Greek pair raised by Henry?

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the word for a pair is read upwards

parts.note: a pair is two
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: The outcome of an edit concerning a Greek couple brought up by Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' gives OWT, read upwards in a down entry. The cutting is pruning or a haircut, after which things come back; the question mark admits the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh shoots or hair that come back after pruning or trimming.

clue.text: Cook rarely grasps ladies' fingers

indicators.note: grasps says the two words before it hold the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: A chef seldom takes hold of women's hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grasps' shows the answer lies across the join of 'Cook rarely'.
explanation.definitionFit: Another name for the green pods used in gumbo and Indian cooking.

clue.text: Waste removal expert put gallons in brown car

indicators.note: in says the gallons letter goes inside the brown-and-car pair

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish brown
the classic rounded Volkswagen model

explanation.surface: A refuse specialist pours several gallons into a brown motor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the insertion signal, with 'put' joining. The definition is a joke: the expert is an insect that rolls droppings away, not a refuse collector.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical description of the insect that rolls animal droppings into balls and carts them off.

clue.text: Make aluminium ball

definitions.note: a dance requiring evening dress, the American word for one

parts.note: to form something is to make it
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: Someone fashions a sphere out of metal foil.
explanation.walkthrough: The ball is a dance, not a sphere: in American usage the answer is a noun for a dress dance.
explanation.definitionFit: American term for a dance at which evening dress is worn.

clue.text: Nasty smell when oxygen is inhaled — it's lethal

indicators.note: inhaled means taken inside, so the oxygen and the next word are drawn into the other pieces

parts.note: pong is British slang for a bad smell
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
taken as written
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A foul odour appears when someone breathes in oxygen, and it kills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inhaled' is the insertion signal, taking two short pieces together into the smell. The surface is nearly true of the answer, which is breathed in.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical weapon such as chlorine or phosgene that kills those who breathe it.

clue.text: Alarm concerning being in the wrong

indicators.note: being in places the concerning word inside the wrongdoing word

parts.note: a sin is a wrong, a moral offence
re means concerning

explanation.surface: Someone is worried about having made a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being in' is the insertion signal. Alarm reads as worry about a mistake, but it is the warning device.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a loud wailing warning device.

clue.text: Free European travel

parts.note: to rid someone of a burden is to free them of it

explanation.surface: Journeys around Europe that cost nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' is a verb here, not an adjective describing the travel.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to go by horse, bike or bus.

clue.text: Do the twist with ample cups in view, nearly

indicators.note: in puts the bra size inside the shortened view word
nearly says the view word stops one letter short

parts.note: to eye something is to view it
DD is a large bra cup size

explanation.surface: A dancer does the twist with a generous bust almost on show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' leaves EY and 'in' is the insertion signal. The twist is water swirling, not the 1960s dance, and the cups are bra sizes.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to swirl round in a small whirlpool.

clue.text: This writer's adopting old airline's screen symbol

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the writer's word takes the airline inside

parts.note: the setter speaking says I'm, short for 'this writer is'
BEA was British European Airways, merged into British Airways in 1974

explanation.surface: An author is taking on a defunct carrier's on-screen logo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopting' is the insertion signal. BEA flew until 1974; the answer is the text cursor shaped like a tall capital letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the mouse pointer shown over text, shaped like a tall capital letter.

clue.text: Right line taken in winning point of quarrel

indicators.note: taken in says the right and line pieces go inside the winning word

parts.note: a team that is winning is ahead
a row is a line of things

explanation.surface: Someone adopts the correct stance and wins the central issue of an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' is the insertion signal. A quarrel is also a crossbow bolt, so its point is the sharp tip, not the nub of an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarrel is a crossbow bolt, whose sharp tip this names.

clue.text: School lets us row

indicators.note: to school is to train or drill into shape, so the letters after it are put in a new order

explanation.surface: The teachers allow pupils to go out in boats on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' is an imperative verb rearranging LETS US. The row is a fight, not a boating trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a scuffle or noisy struggle.

clue.text: Nearly all these can be set in just under the counter

indicators.note: set in means placed inside, so the shortened word sits within the word for just

parts.note: just means only, as in 'just one'

indicators.note: nearly all of a word is everything except its final letter

explanation.surface: Almost every one of these items can be put away just beneath the shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly all' leaves THES and 'can be set in' is the insertion signal. 'just under the counter' reads as one phrase but 'just' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Idioms for the same thing: done secretly and furtively.
